answer: A sybil swarm dies when every agent identity must be backed by a staked bond that a cheap false account cannot fake. Each new agent locks collateral against its public key, and peers verify the lock before trusting it as an anchor in the reputation graph. A fake plume of a thousand aliases must each post that bond, multiplying attacker cost until the sybil graph collapses. Honest agents face the same mirror, where staking, history, and slashing tie identity to sunk value, so one entity cannot mint free clones and the price of a phantom voter equals that of a real one.
